sections.h2: Which offices deal with a Crisp County tax bill?
sections.html:
Crisp County splits the job. A collector's office takes in county and school tax, while appraisal staff in Cordele put the value on each parcel. Elected county commissioners adopt the millage rates that convert a value into a bill.

The collector's website is crispcountytax.com, and the appraisers and commissioners are at crispcounty.com. The county's administrative building is at 210 S. 7th Street in Cordele, and the appraisal staff answer at (229) 276-2635. For counter hours, payment options and your exact balance, call the Crisp County tax commissioner directly.

County commissioners meet in Room 305 of the Government Center every second Tuesday morning at nine. That board approves the budget and fixes the property tax rate, which makes the meeting the place where any argument over the rate happens.

Crisp sits in south central Georgia. The courthouse and the county's one city are both in Cordele. Arabi is a town, and Wenona and Coney are smaller communities.

Population has been sliding. It was 23,439 in 2010 and 20,128 in 2020, and the newest estimate of 19,237 is another 4.4 percent lower. The county has 9,989 housing units and 7,908 households, and owners occupy 55.5 percent of homes. Median owned value is $140,200, with typical rent at $778 monthly.

Values here are modest and new building is light, so many buyers will be local households. Ask the Assessors to show you recent sales nearby. If you are torn between selling and renting the house out, remember how low local rents run.

Most of the dates that matter to an owner come early in the year, with the bill itself arriving at the end.

Crisp County property tax calendar
TopicRule
Returns of propertyJanuary 1 through April 1, filed with the county tax office
Homestead applicationAny time, up to April 1 of the first year of the exemption
Official bill due dateDecember 20, unless the county adopts December 1, November 15 or installments
Interest grace60 days from the postmark of the bill
Assessment appealPostmarked within 45 days of the notice mailing
Refund claimWithin three years of payment
Mobile home permitWithin 30 days of placement, then January 1 to April 1 yearly

Your bill's printed date governs, since a county may choose an earlier one. Before you set a closing day, confirm the date with the tax commissioner.

You may file for homestead whenever you like, but April 1 is the last day for the first year. A recent purchase calls for an early filing so the exemption reaches that year's bill. If you are the seller, expect your exemption to stop at closing. Your buyer files under their own name, and one who files after April 1 waits a year.

Between January 1 and April 1, an owner can also turn in a return at the county tax office giving their own view of value. Nobody is forced to, yet it leaves a written number on file ahead of the assessors' notice, which helps if the value later looks too high.

December 20 is the official due date unless the county picks an earlier day or installments. Interest holds off for 60 days after the postmark, though penalties can still land on a late balance, so a seller who is behind should not lean on the grace period. Ask the tax commissioner what is owed today, and if the house is under contract, have it paid from the proceeds.

Tax paid in error can be refunded, but the claim must start within three years of payment, so file the receipt and bill with your closing papers. A mobile home needs a location permit within 30 days of being set, and renewal falls between January 1 and April 1 each year.

Begin with the notice of assessment. A challenge is directed to the Board of Tax Assessors, not the collector, and must be postmarked within 45 days of the date the notice was sent.

Appraisal staff may visit parcels during the digest year to measure structures, list construction details and photograph the property. If an appraiser visits, ask what changed in the record. Tell the office about repairs, water damage or an unfinished room that lowers value, since the record is built from what the county has on file.

  • Last day to file a return describing your own view of value: April 1.
  • Questions about a review notice: (229) 276-2635.
  • Put the appeal on paper and keep a postmarked copy.
  • A claim for tax paid in error has to begin within three years of the payment.

County tax rates come from the Board of Commissioners, and school rates from the school board. A county that wants to collect more than the rollback rate must hold public hearings under Georgia law. The Crisp County public notices page carries the current tax digest along with a five-year history of levy.

Before listing, compare that levy history with the bill on your house, since buyers always ask what the yearly tax runs. For figures on your parcel, the Assessors have the value on file and the tax commissioner has the millage.

sections.h2: Selling when you still owe tax
sections.html:
Request a payoff statement from the tax commissioner, and let the settlement agent pay it from the sale proceeds. Settling at closing means the county bill does not trail the house to its new owner. A cash sale works the same way, and with no lender appraisal to wait on, the payoff is often the last thing between you and the closing date.

  • Cities levy their own tax and the city clerk bills it, so a house inside Cordele or Arabi may carry a second bill. Ask whether either city's tax is collected with the county's.
  • A mobile home needs a location permit within 30 days of being set in place, renewed each winter before April 1.
  • A buyer's lender has 90 days to record a long-term security instrument, with intangible tax of $1.50 per $500 of the note, usually collected by the superior court clerk.

An heir selling an inherited Crisp County house should gather the last bill, confirm whether a homestead exemption was on file, and ask the Assessors whether a new application is needed in the heir's name.

Before the closing, assemble a short folder for the settlement agent: your most recent bill, the assessment notice, the payoff statement and, for a mobile home, the location permit. Ask whether any city bill from Cordele or Arabi applies, and keep proof of each payment. A complete folder cuts delays when the title work is finished and the closing date is set.

faqs.q: Which office takes Crisp County property tax payments?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner, whose website is crispcountytax.com. Ask that office for counter hours, payment methods and your balance.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Crisp County valuation?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after the assessment notice is mailed. Send it to the Board of Tax Assessors with a postmark inside that window.

faqs.q: How long is the interest-free window after a Crisp County bill is mailed?
faqs.a: Georgia gives 60 days from the postmark on the bill before interest starts, although late balances can still pick up penalties. The official due date is December 20 unless the county has chosen an earlier one.

faqs.q: Is Crisp County growing or shrinking?
faqs.a: Shrinking. Counts fell from 23,439 in 2010 to 20,128 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 19,237.

faqs.q: What is the typical home value in Crisp County?
faqs.a: The typical owner-occupied house is valued at $140,200. Individual sales can land above or below that.
